name: SalesforceMCP
title: Salesforce
description: Query, read, create and update records in a Salesforce org.
whenToUse: Pick for customer and CRM data in Salesforce: look up customers, accounts, contacts and opportunities, and capture or update leads. Reads any object, SOQL under the hood; writes are lead-only with a fixed field set, so an agent can never modify other records. Attach it via a service edge to an agent, or trigger it directly with a fixed query.

package.name: salesforce
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# FULLY DECLARATIVE. package.yaml, nodes/, credentials/ and shared/, nothing else.
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/salesforce/`.
#
# This is HubSpot's twin and it migrated on the same capabilities, plus one of its own:
# `oauth2ClientCredentials`. Salesforce does not take an API key. It exchanges a connected
# app's id and secret for a short-lived token over a form-encoded POST, and the org's data
# lives at the `instance_url` that exchange returns rather than at the host you
# authenticated against. All of that is computation over the request, so it is an executor
# auth scheme and every OAuth2 client-credentials API after this one inherits it.

name: salesforce
displayName: Salesforce
description: Salesforce CRM integration for Unoverse
version: 2.0.0
category: productivity
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1781672225/gravity/icons/Salesforce-dark.svg

features:
  - SOQL queries and record reads
  - Lead create and update, a fixed field set
  - Resolve the signed-in user to a Contact or Lead
  - Append-only insight Tasks

# Per-org My Domain hosts, plus the two Salesforce login domains a token is minted at.
# One subdomain level only, which is what the pattern means.
allowedHosts:
  - "*.my.salesforce.com"
  - login.salesforce.com
  - test.salesforce.com

requires:
  credential: [oauth2ClientCredentials]
  transport: [json]
  state: [merge, drain]
  executorVersion: ">=1.2.0"

credentials.salesforceOAuth.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# Transcribed from src/credentials/index.ts. The SHAPE only; values live encrypted in
# Postgres on a deployed universe and in the developer's .env locally.

name: salesforceOAuth
displayName: Salesforce
description: >-
  Salesforce connected app, OAuth2 client credentials. The executor exchanges these for a
  short-lived access token at run time and caches it, so this acts as one integration
  identity rather than as a person.
documentationUrl: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.connected_app_client_credentials_setup.htm

properties:
  - name: host
    displayName: Login / My Domain URL
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Your Salesforce My Domain or login URL, used for the OAuth token endpoint
    placeholder: https://your-org.my.salesforce.com

  - name: clientId
    displayName: Consumer Key (Client ID)
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Connected app Consumer Key
    placeholder: 3MVG9...

  - name: clientSecret
    displayName: Consumer Secret (Client Secret)
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Connected app Consumer Secret
    placeholder: ""

  - name: apiVersion
    displayName: API Version
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Salesforce REST API version. Defaults to v52.0.
    placeholder: v52.0

shared.api.yaml:
# The two things every Salesforce call needs: how to authenticate, and where to send it.
#
# Referenced by every call in the node, so an API version bump or an auth change is one
# edit here rather than ten.

# The connected app exchange. The executor mints the token, form-encodes the request,
# caches it per app until it expires, and refreshes once on a 401. A manifest cannot
# express any of that, which is why it is a scheme rather than a call.
credential: &credential
  scheme: oauth2ClientCredentials
  tokenUrl: "{{ credentials.salesforceOAuth.host }}/services/oauth2/token"
  clientId: "{{ credentials.salesforceOAuth.clientId }}"
  clientSecret: "{{ credentials.salesforceOAuth.clientSecret }}"

# `token.instanceUrl` is what the exchange returned, and the org's data lives THERE rather
# than at the host you authenticated against. An expression rather than a template, because
# apiVersion is optional and `{{ }}` resolving to empty would produce `/services/data//`.
#
# These are the path prefixes; each call appends its own resource.
query: &queryUrl >-
  return token.instanceUrl + '/services/data/'
    + (credentials.salesforceOAuth.apiVersion || 'v52.0') + '/query'

sobjects: &sobjectsUrl >-
  return token.instanceUrl + '/services/data/'
    + (credentials.salesforceOAuth.apiVersion || 'v52.0') + '/sobjects/'
shared.contact.yaml:
# Resolving the signed-in person, and the bounded profile that comes back.
#
# Salesforce needs TWO lookups where HubSpot needed one: a person is a Contact, or if not,
# an unconverted Lead. A converted lead IS its Contact, so it must not match twice.
#
# SOQL is assembled as a string, so every interpolated value is escaped. split/join rather
# than a regex, because the expression sandbox takes no regex literal.

# ── the calls ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

contact: &contact
  name: contact
  method: GET
  url: { $ref: api#query }
  credential: { $ref: api#credential }
  query:
    q: >-
      return "SELECT Id, Name, FirstName, LastName, Email, Title, Phone, Account.Name FROM Contact WHERE Email = '"
        + String(params.email || user.email || '').split('\\').join('\\\\').split("'").join("\\'")
        + "' LIMIT 1"
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

# Only when no Contact matched. A skipped call leaves no key, which is what `result` tests.
lead: &lead
  name: lead
  when: "return ((calls.contact || {}).records || []).length === 0"
  method: GET
  url: { $ref: api#query }
  credential: { $ref: api#credential }
  query:
    q: >-
      return "SELECT Id, Name, FirstName, LastName, Email, Title, Phone, Company FROM Lead WHERE Email = '"
        + String(params.email || user.email || '').split('\\').join('\\\\').split("'").join("\\'")
        + "' AND IsConverted = false ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC LIMIT 1"
  transport: json

# The identity snapshot the memory server reads. MERGE, because it writes its own fields
# into the same key. Skipped where there is no workflow scope to key on.
cache: &cache
  name: cache
  state: merge
  when: "return !!scope.userId && !!scope.workflowId"
  key: "crm:{{ scope.userId }}:{{ scope.workflowId }}"
  value: >-
    return { contact: [].concat(
      ((calls.contact || {}).records || []).map(r => ({
        id: r.Id, name: r.Name || null, email: r.Email || null,
        company: (r.Account || {}).Name || null, kind: 'contact'
      })),
      ((calls.lead || {}).records || []).map(r => ({
        id: r.Id, name: r.Name || null, email: r.Email || null,
        company: r.Company || null, kind: 'lead'
      }))
    )[0] || null }

# Hydrate: the memory server queues high-certainty deductions here and the connector writes
# them back as append-only Tasks. Items are POPPED, so a re-run cannot duplicate them.
hydrate: &hydrate
  name: hydrate
  state: drain
  when: >-
    return config.syncUser === true
      && (((calls.contact || {}).records || []).length > 0
       || ((calls.lead || {}).records || []).length > 0)
  key: "crm:hydrate:{{ scope.userId }}:{{ scope.workflowId }}"
  max: 25

# One composite call rather than a Task create per item. Subject is capped at 255 by
# Salesforce, so the full text goes in Description and the subject is truncated.
hydrateTasks: &hydrateTasks
  name: hydrateTasks
  when: "return (calls.hydrate || []).length > 0"
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return token.instanceUrl + '/services/data/'
      + (credentials.salesforceOAuth.apiVersion || 'v52.0') + '/composite/sobjects'
  credential: { $ref: api#credential }
  body: >-
    return {
      allOrNone: false,
      records: calls.hydrate.filter(i => i && i.claim).map(i => ({
        attributes: { type: 'Task' },
        Subject: i.claim.length > 255 ? i.claim.slice(0, 252) + '…' : i.claim,
        Status: 'Completed',
        Priority: 'Normal',
        WhoId: (((calls.contact || {}).records || []).concat(((calls.lead || {}).records || []))[0] || {}).Id,
        Description: 'Gravity AI — machine-authored, unverified'
          + (i.certainty ? ' (certainty ' + Math.round(i.certainty * 100) + '%)' : '')
          + '\n\n' + i.claim
      }))
    }
  transport: json

# ── the sequences ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

resolve: [*contact, *lead]
resolveAndCache: [*contact, *lead, *cache]
sync: [*contact, *lead, *cache, *hydrate, *hydrateTasks]

# ── what a caller gets back ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A FIXED field list, never SELECT *. A Contact wins over a Lead, and `company` comes from
# the associated Account for a Contact but sits directly on a Lead.
#
# A miss is `found: false`, never an error: a person who is not in the CRM is the normal
# case, and an agent that treats it as a failure stops the conversation dead.
result: >-
  return [[].concat(
    ((calls.contact || {}).records || []).map(r => ({
      id: r.Id,
      name: r.Name || null,
      firstName: r.FirstName || null,
      lastName: r.LastName || null,
      email: r.Email || null,
      title: r.Title || null,
      phone: r.Phone || null,
      company: (r.Account || {}).Name || null,
      kind: 'contact'
    })),
    ((calls.lead || {}).records || []).map(r => ({
      id: r.Id,
      name: r.Name || null,
      firstName: r.FirstName || null,
      lastName: r.LastName || null,
      email: r.Email || null,
      title: r.Title || null,
      phone: r.Phone || null,
      company: r.Company || null,
      kind: 'lead'
    }))
  )[0] || null].map(p => ({ ok: true, found: !!p, contact: p }))[0]

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order. One connector, one row.
#
# The node does one of two jobs depending on `syncUser`, so the row picks: the resolved
# contact profile when syncing, otherwise the query result.

- emit: output
  from: response
  value: >-
    return config.syncUser === true
      ? { ok: true,
          found: (((calls.contact || {}).records || []).length
                + ((calls.lead || {}).records || []).length) > 0,
          hydrated: (calls.hydrate || []).length }
      : { ok: true,
          totalSize: (calls.query || {}).totalSize,
          records: ((calls.query || {}).records) || [],
          has_more: (calls.query || {}).done === false,
          next_records_url: (calls.query || {}).nextRecordsUrl || null }
files.api/run.yaml:
# The WORKFLOW channel. The node does ONE of two jobs, chosen by `syncUser`, and every call
# is gated so the unused branch sends nothing.
#
# Sync on:  resolve the person, cache them, drain the insight queue, write the Tasks.
# Sync off: run the query, from the upstream input if it carried one, else the configured
#           default.

- { $ref: contact#contact, when: "return config.syncUser === true" }
- { $ref: contact#lead }
- { $ref: contact#cache }
- { $ref: contact#hydrate }
- { $ref: contact#hydrateTasks }

# Only a NON-EMPTY STRING counts as a query. A wired upstream node often puts an object on
# `input`, and stringifying that would send "[object Object]" to Salesforce; the retired
# code had the same guard for the same reason.
- name: query
  when: >-
    return config.syncUser !== true
      && !!(typeof (signal.input || {}).soql === 'string' && (signal.input || {}).soql.trim()
            ? (signal.input || {}).soql.trim()
            : String(config.defaultQuery || '').trim())
  method: GET
  url: { $ref: api#query }
  credential: { $ref: api#credential }
  query:
    q: >-
      return typeof (signal.input || {}).soql === 'string' && (signal.input || {}).soql.trim()
        ? (signal.input || {}).soql.trim()
        : String(config.defaultQuery || '').trim()
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
files.api/service.yaml:
# The MCP methods an agent can call ad-hoc. Transcribed from src/SalesforceMCP/service/.
#
# The shape of the surface is deliberate and is the security model: READS are general (any
# object, via SOQL), WRITES are Leads only with a fixed field list. An agent cannot modify
# an Account, an Opportunity or a converted Contact, because no method here can.
#
# Descriptions are what a model reads when choosing a tool, so they say what comes back and
# what an empty result means.

query_records:
  description: >-
    Run a SOQL query and return the first page of records. Use for any read: contacts,
    accounts, opportunities, custom objects. Returns has_more and next_records_url when the
    result was truncated.
  calls:
    - name: query
      method: GET
      url: { $ref: api#query }
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      query:
        q: "{{ params.soql }}"
      transport: json
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      totalSize: response.totalSize,
      records: response.records || [],
      has_more: response.done === false,
      next_records_url: response.nextRecordsUrl || null
    }

get_record:
  description: >-
    Fetch one record by its Salesforce id. Pass a comma-separated `fields` list to bound
    what comes back; omit it for the default field set.
  calls:
    - name: record
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return token.instanceUrl + '/services/data/'
          + (credentials.salesforceOAuth.apiVersion || 'v52.0')
          + '/sobjects/' + encodeURIComponent(params.sobject)
          + '/' + encodeURIComponent(params.recordId)
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      query:
        fields: "{{ params.fields }}"
      transport: json
  returns: "return { ok: true, record: response }"

create_lead:
  description: >-
    Create a Lead. lastName and company are required by Salesforce. Only the standard lead
    fields can be set; this cannot create any other kind of record.
  calls:
    - name: lead
      method: POST
      url: >-
        return token.instanceUrl + '/services/data/'
          + (credentials.salesforceOAuth.apiVersion || 'v52.0') + '/sobjects/Lead/'
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      # Empty and null are dropped, not sent: a strict tool schema fills unused fields with
      # null, and Salesforce rejects null on a picklist.
      body: >-
        return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
          FirstName: params.firstName,
          LastName: params.lastName,
          Company: params.company,
          Email: params.email,
          Phone: params.phone,
          Title: params.title,
          Website: params.website,
          LeadSource: params.leadSource,
          Industry: params.industry,
          Description: params.description
        }).filter(e => e[1] !== undefined && e[1] !== null && e[1] !== ''))
      transport: json
  returns: "return { ok: !!response.success, id: response.id || null, errors: response.errors || [] }"

update_lead:
  description: >-
    Update the Lead matching an email address, the most recent if several. Refuses a
    converted lead, which is a Contact and read-only here. Returns NOT_FOUND when no lead
    has that email.
  calls:
    - name: found
      method: GET
      url: { $ref: api#query }
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      query:
        q: >-
          return "SELECT Id, IsConverted FROM Lead WHERE Email = '"
            + String(params.email || '').split('\\').join('\\\\').split("'").join("\\'")
            + "' ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC LIMIT 1"
      transport: json

    # Only when a lead was found AND it has not converted. Email is the lookup key, so it is
    # never one of the fields written back.
    - name: updated
      when: >-
        return (calls.found.records || []).filter(r => !r.IsConverted).length > 0
          && Object.keys(Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
              FirstName: params.firstName, LastName: params.lastName, Company: params.company,
              Phone: params.phone, Title: params.title, Website: params.website,
              LeadSource: params.leadSource, Industry: params.industry, Description: params.description
            }).filter(e => e[1] !== undefined && e[1] !== null && e[1] !== ''))).length > 0
      method: PATCH
      url: >-
        return token.instanceUrl + '/services/data/'
          + (credentials.salesforceOAuth.apiVersion || 'v52.0')
          + '/sobjects/Lead/' + encodeURIComponent(calls.found.records[0].Id)
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      body: >-
        return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
          FirstName: params.firstName,
          LastName: params.lastName,
          Company: params.company,
          Phone: params.phone,
          Title: params.title,
          Website: params.website,
          LeadSource: params.leadSource,
          Industry: params.industry,
          Description: params.description
        }).filter(e => e[1] !== undefined && e[1] !== null && e[1] !== ''))
      transport: json
  # Each refusal names itself and says what to do instead, because a model reads this.
  returns: >-
    return (calls.found.records || []).length === 0
      ? { ok: false, error: 'NOT_FOUND', hint: 'No lead with that email. Use create_lead first.' }
      : calls.found.records[0].IsConverted
        ? { ok: false, error: 'LEAD_CONVERTED', hint: 'This lead was converted to a Contact and cannot be updated through this tool.' }
        : !calls.updated
          ? { ok: false, error: 'NO_FIELDS', hint: 'Provide at least one field to change.' }
          : { ok: true, id: calls.found.records[0].Id }

describe_object:
  description: >-
    An object's fields and metadata: name, label, type, whether it is required or
    updateable, and any picklist values. Use before writing to learn what a field accepts.
  calls:
    - name: describe
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return token.instanceUrl + '/services/data/'
          + (credentials.salesforceOAuth.apiVersion || 'v52.0')
          + '/sobjects/' + encodeURIComponent(params.sobject) + '/describe/'
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      transport: json
  # The full describe payload is enormous. This is the part an agent reasons about.
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      name: response.name,
      label: response.label,
      fields: (response.fields || []).map(f => ({
        name: f.name,
        label: f.label,
        type: f.type,
        required: f.nillable === false && f.defaultedOnCreate === false,
        updateable: f.updateable,
        picklistValues: (f.picklistValues || []).map(p => p.value)
      }))
    }

list_objects:
  description: The objects this org has, and whether each is queryable, createable or updateable.
  calls:
    - name: objects
      method: GET
      url: { $ref: api#sobjects }
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      transport: json
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      sobjects: (response.sobjects || []).map(s => ({
        name: s.name, label: s.label,
        queryable: s.queryable, createable: s.createable, updateable: s.updateable
      }))
    }

# ── the CRM sync contract (CRM_SYNC.md) ──────────────────────────────────────────

crm_resolve_user:
  description: >-
    Resolve a user to their CRM record and bounded identity profile. Pass an email to look
    that person up; omit it for the currently authenticated user. Matches a Contact first,
    then an unconverted Lead. An empty result means they are not in the CRM, which is
    normal: just proceed.
  calls: { $ref: contact#resolveAndCache }
  returns: { $ref: contact#result }

crm_get_profile:
  description: The bounded identity profile for a known record id. Never a full record dump.
  calls:
    - name: contact
      method: GET
      url: { $ref: api#query }
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      query:
        q: >-
          return "SELECT Id, Name, FirstName, LastName, Email, Title, Phone, Account.Name FROM Contact WHERE Id = '"
            + String(params.contactId || '').split('\\').join('\\\\').split("'").join("\\'")
            + "' LIMIT 1"
      transport: json
  returns: >-
    return [(response.records || []).map(r => ({
      id: r.Id, name: r.Name || null, firstName: r.FirstName || null, lastName: r.LastName || null,
      email: r.Email || null, title: r.Title || null, phone: r.Phone || null,
      company: (r.Account || {}).Name || null
    }))[0] || null].map(p => ({ ok: !!p, profile: p }))[0]

crm_write_insight:
  description: >-
    Append a durable, machine-authored insight about a person to their CRM record, as a
    completed Task. APPEND-ONLY: it never edits an existing field. Push only high-certainty
    conclusions.
  calls:
    - name: task
      method: POST
      url: >-
        return token.instanceUrl + '/services/data/'
          + (credentials.salesforceOAuth.apiVersion || 'v52.0') + '/sobjects/Task/'
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      # Subject is capped at 255 by Salesforce, so the full text lives in Description and
      # the subject is truncated. The stamp is a WIRE MARKER: crm_read_insights matches on
      # it, so its wording is fixed and must not be tidied.
      body: >-
        return {
          Subject: params.insight.length > 255 ? params.insight.slice(0, 252) + '…' : params.insight,
          Status: 'Completed',
          Priority: 'Normal',
          WhoId: params.contactId,
          Description: 'Gravity AI — machine-authored, unverified'
            + (params.certainty ? ' (certainty ' + Math.round(params.certainty * 100) + '%)' : '')
            + '\n\n' + params.insight
        }
      transport: json
  returns: "return { ok: !!response.success, id: response.id || null }"

crm_read_insights:
  description: The machine-authored insights previously written about this person, newest first.
  calls:
    - name: tasks
      method: GET
      url: { $ref: api#query }
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      query:
        q: >-
          return "SELECT Id, Subject, Description, CreatedDate FROM Task WHERE WhoId = '"
            + String(params.contactId || '').split('\\').join('\\\\').split("'").join("\\'")
            + "' AND Description LIKE 'Gravity AI%' ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC LIMIT "
            + Math.min(Math.max(params.limit || 50, 1), 200)
      transport: json
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      insights: (response.records || []).map(t => ({
        id: t.Id, subject: t.Subject, description: t.Description, createdDate: t.CreatedDate
      }))
    }
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    syncUser:
      type: boolean
      title: Sync user on trigger
      description: >-
        On trigger, resolve the signed-in user, refresh their cached profile, and write back
        any insight Tasks the memory server has queued. Leave off to run a query instead.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    defaultQuery:
      type: string
      title: Default SOQL Query
      description: >-
        SOQL run when the workflow triggers this node directly. Not used for MCP tool calls
        or when Sync user is on. An upstream { soql } on the input wins over this.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:dependencies": { syncUser: false }

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order": [authRequired, authRole, syncUser, defaultQuery]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: Trigger input. Optionally { soql } to run a query instead of the configured one.

outputs:
  - name: output
    type: object
    description: >-
      What the node ran. A query result when Sync user is off, the resolved contact profile
      when it is on.

credentials:
  - name: salesforceOAuth
    required: true
    displayName: Salesforce

serviceConnectors:
  - name: mcpService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: true
    methods:
      - query_records
      - get_record
      - create_lead
      - update_lead
      - describe_object
      - list_objects
      - crm_resolve_user
      - crm_get_profile
      - crm_write_insight
      - crm_read_insights
    description: >-
      MCP tools for an agent: SOQL queries, record reads, lead create and update, object
      metadata, and the CRM sync contract (resolve the signed-in user, read their profile,
      append an insight, read insights back).
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: SalesforceMCP
kind: PromiseNode
name: Salesforce
category: Go To Market
color: "#00A1E0"
# Attached to an agent over a service edge rather than wired in sequence.
template: service
description: Query, read, create and update records in a Salesforce org.
whenToUse: >
  Pick for customer and CRM data in Salesforce: look up customers, accounts, contacts and
  opportunities, and capture or update leads. Reads any object, SOQL under the hood; writes
  are lead-only with a fixed field set, so an agent can never modify other records. Attach
  it via a service edge to an agent, or trigger it directly with a fixed query.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Not cacheable: CRM records change underneath us, and the write methods have side
  # effects that reuse would silently skip.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# The READ path, because it is the one that proves the OAuth exchange, the instance_url and
# the SOQL all work. The write methods are deliberately not the fixture: they would leave a
# real Lead and a real Task behind, and a bench that litters is one nobody runs twice.
testData:
  config:
    syncUser: false
    defaultQuery: SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 3

  inputs:
    input: {}

  expect:
    # Any org answers this. Asserting a row count would tie the fixture to one org's data.
    output: >-
      return output.output.ok === true && Array.isArray(output.output.records)
